title: First-order equations
description: Read a local rule, find a solution, and explore how a model behaves.

examples.title: From fluids to ODEs
examples.description: Track a particle in a swirling field, then ask whether a solution can last forever.
examples.label: Motion & finite-time blowup

examples.title: Follow the slope
examples.description: Predict, sketch, and reveal a solution. Change the initial condition and compare trajectories.
examples.label: y′ = t − y

examples.title: Position, velocity & acceleration
examples.description: Follow a moving particle and connect its position, velocity, and acceleration. Does positive acceleration always mean speeding up?
examples.label: x′ = v · v′ = a

examples.title: Two drops on Planet Gzyx
examples.description: Infer gravity from one observed fall, then predict how height changes the fall time and impact speed.
examples.label: 20 ft in 2 s → 200 ft?

examples.title: From a grid to solution curves
examples.description: Sample a grid, add local slopes, and follow a solution. Compare grid density with the step size of a tangent-step approximation.
examples.label: Grid → slopes → solution

examples.title: Match two areas
examples.description: Separate the variables, match accumulated areas, and build a solution one point at a time.
examples.label: y′ = ty

examples.title: From a field to a particular solution
examples.description: Explore the three Lecture 04 equations. Choose an initial point, reveal its curve, and check equilibria, domains, and implicit branches.
examples.label: Three equations · choose an initial value

examples.title: What does an integrating factor change?
examples.description: Follow the Lecture 05 solution through (1, 10), then compare y with z = y/x³ and see how the slope field changes.
examples.label: xy′ − 3y = x³ · y(1) = 10

examples.title: Follow a curve. Keep F constant.
examples.description: Overlay contours and a slope field, follow either solution branch, and watch a changing point keep the same value of F.
examples.label: M dx + N dy = dF = 0

examples.title: AI Self-Improvement Simulator
examples.description: Change the relative self-improvement rate, cross a threshold, and compare exponential growth, logistic saturation, and finite-time blow-up.
examples.label: A′ = A k(A)

examples.title: What happens near equilibrium?
examples.description: Connect a separate phase line to solution curves. Explore stable, unstable, and semistable equilibria.
examples.label: x′ = x²(x² − 4)

examples.title: Take one small step
examples.description: Build an approximation one tangent step at a time, compare h with h/2, and reveal the exact solution.
examples.label: yₙ₊₁ = yₙ + h f(xₙ, yₙ)

title: Higher-order linear equations
description: Combine solutions, follow an oscillator, and discover the role of forcing and boundaries.

examples.title: Two initial conditions, one solution
examples.description: Fix a starting value, explore a family of curves, and add the initial slope to select one solution.
examples.label: y(0) + y′(0) → one solution

examples.title: Which exponential solves the ODE?
examples.description: Adjust r in an exponential trial function. Match the two sides of the ODE and connect that match to a root of the characteristic polynomial.
examples.label: y = eʳˣ · p(r) = 0

examples.title: Why do we need two independent solutions?
examples.description: Try to match an initial value and slope. Connect linear independence to two arrows and the area measured by the Wronskian.
examples.label: y = c₁y₁ + c₂y₂ · area = |W|

examples.title: One multiplier, one whole interval
examples.description: Compare x³ and x²|x| on three intervals. Find a constant multiplier and explore what a zero Wronskian can and cannot tell us.
examples.label: f(x) = x³ · g(x) = x²|x|

examples.title: One particular solution. A whole family.
examples.description: Add a homogeneous solution to a particular solution, check the differential equation, and change the decomposition while preserving the total curve.
examples.label: y″ − 4y = 12 · two constants

examples.title: Set an oscillator in motion
examples.description: Explore natural frequency, damping, and the transition between different kinds of motion.

examples.title: Add a driving force
examples.description: Separate transient and forced responses in a nonhomogeneous equation.

examples.title: Find the resonant frequency
examples.description: Change the driving frequency and observe the oscillator's response.

examples.title: Meet both boundaries
examples.description: Vary an eigenvalue parameter until a solution satisfies both endpoint conditions.

title: Linear systems
description: Let matrices shape motion, and read solutions through eigenvalues and the phase plane.

examples.title: Two variables, one motion
examples.description: Rewrite an oscillator as a first-order system and track its state in the plane.

examples.title: Follow an eigendirection
examples.description: Connect matrix action, eigenvectors, and the growth or decay of a solution.

examples.title: Read the phase portrait
examples.description: Compare nodes, saddles, spirals, and centers through their trajectories.

examples.title: Same eigenvalues, different motion
examples.description: See how an incomplete set of eigenvectors changes the geometry of a flow.

examples.title: Drive a coupled system
examples.description: Combine a system's natural evolution with an external input.
